title: This Tiny Animal Survived Naked in Outer Space 🐻 #shorts
description:
Tardigrades, or "water bears", are eight-legged animals only about half a millimetre long. In 2007, ESA's FOTON-M3 mission exposed dried-out tardigrades to open space for 10 days in low Earth orbit, around 270 km up – and many came back to life when rehydrated, some even laying eggs. They can also survive cold down to about -200 °C, and in 2014 Japanese scientists revived tardigrades frozen in Antarctic moss for more than 30 years.

Sources: ESA, National Geographic, Scientific American, Space.com, CBC News, Gizmodo, Carleton College SERC, UC ANR

scenes.label: TINY WATER BEAR

scenes.text: Discovered in seventeen seventy three. In two thousand seven, Europe's space agency sent them into orbit.
Dried-out water bears rode outside a capsule, exposed to the vacuum and the sun's radiation.
Back on Earth, scientists added water. Many woke up. Some even laid eggs!
They also survive cold down to minus two hundred degrees Celsius.
Their secret? They dry out, curl into a ball called a tun, and almost shut down.
In twenty fourteen, scientists woke up water bears frozen in Antarctic moss for over thirty years.
